survivingClaim: No new result; precise obstruction. (i) C intersect A = {zeta} is Hamburger's theorem (classical; cone and multiplicativity unused), and geometric means of zeta translates fail A at the gamma-factor poles (proved, re-derived). (ii) Lattice translates zeta(s + 2 pi i k/log(Tc/2 pi)) are unitary cone elements whose defect in zeta's functional equation on [T,T+H] is at most (|alpha|H + alpha^2)/(2T) times |zeta| to leading order (re-derived; confirmed directly to T = 2e8), so a one-window tolerance version admits a unimodular-twist control over a range of alpha that grows with T. (iii) In the lane's float64 finite model (not certified), one window imposes about 30 real conditions and does not exclude a prescribed zero at 3/4 + i t0 at tolerance 1e-5 for T = 3e4 (referee run), 1e5, 1e6; the multi-height constraint pins F(s0) (slice and first order only) with a constant that grows with T, which only says F equals zeta in the window. Nothing is established about zeros of zeta.
obstruction: Exact uniqueness is Hamburger's theorem and uses neither the cone nor multiplicativity. In one window [T,T+H], lattice translates zeta(s + 2 pi i k/log(T/2pi)) are cone elements with functional-equation defect about (|alpha|H + alpha^2)/(2T), so the feasible set at fixed tolerance grows with T; a window gives about 30 real conditions against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes, and a prescribed zero at 3/4 + i t0 is feasible (float64 model, T up to 1e6). The multi-height constraint only says F equals zeta in the window.
controlsThatDefeat: lattice height translates of zeta (unimodular twists; pass every single-window functional-equation test)
L(s, chi_5) at height T/5 (residual about 50/T, measured)

lesson: The functional equation is linear in a(n) and the Euler cone is convex in log F, so "cone intersect affine space" holds in no single variable. A window of length H gives about 30 to 35 real conditions independent of T, against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes; pinning in one window needs H of Riemann-Siegel size. Windowed functional-equation tests cannot separate zeta from its lattice translates or from L(s, chi_5) at height T/5 (measured residual about 50/T). Stability around zeta can never exclude zeros uniformly because inf |zeta(3/4+it)| = 0. Multiplicativity only reduces N unknowns to pi(N) (cone pinned, relaxed model unpinned at T = 1e5 in the multi-height model).
followUp: None on this route. If kept at all: record the window-translate lemma (zeta translates and shifted L-functions pass any single-window functional-equation test) as a new control in OBSTRUCTION_MAP section 2, since it kills any attack whose functional-equation input is local in height.
